label: Lower-volume consolidation of hip-turn control
effort: Produce a short clean rotational kick from a simple base while reducing landing and strength volume.
brief: This is a workload consolidation, not a claim that unfamiliar drills are already mastered. Supporting tasks simplify balance or remove large travel: ankle-led release, leg-driven turning without an arm swing, a low outward sweep, a retreat plant and supported return-direction hip torque.
marker: valid E2 attempts out of four per leg from the same parallel stance, with one weight shift, no extra step and a controlled low finish.

e.name: Supported calf-pop to low knee chamber
e.execution: With fingertip bench support, keep the support knee softly bent and make a brisk heel rise while bringing the opposite bent knee to a low chamber. The supporting forefoot stays down; no hop or large turn. Lower and reset.
e.job: Coordinate the ankle-led heel release with unloading the free leg, without another landing.
e.gate: Use a smaller heel rise/chamber instead if the ankle rolls or the forefoot leaves the floor.
e.novelty: Ankle-led non-flight rise plus free-leg unloading, distinct from a thigh-led band drive or full hip pivot.

e.name: Parallel-stance low roundhouse
e.execution: Start with both feet parallel in a comfortable athletic stance. Shift onto the support leg and turn its foot/pelvis into one low roundhouse with the other leg; recoil and return to the original parallel base. No preselected front/rear fighting stance or entry step.
e.job: Organize support selection and the hip turn from a neutral two-foot base.
e.gate: Widen the starting base slightly or reduce the kick arc instead if the athlete needs a rescue step; feet must be free to turn.
e.novelty: Neutral parallel start requires support selection rather than the prearranged front/rear loading in earlier full kicks.

e.name: Hands-on-hips rotational jump to stick
e.execution: Keep hands resting on the hips. Use a small natural dip and turn in a low two-foot jump through a controllable arc up to 90 degrees; land aligned and hold 2 s. No arm wind-up or repeated bounce.
e.job: Observe leg/hip-driven rotational takeoff with arm-swing assistance removed.
e.gate: Use a smaller turn instead if removing the arms disrupts landing; do not chase the angle achieved with free arms.
e.novelty: Explicit arm-contribution constraint within the known rotational-jump family; a distinct task condition, not a new unrelated jump pattern.

e.name: Supported low outward crescent sweep
e.execution: With light fingertip support, start the low free foot near the midline and sweep it outward in a small arc with a soft knee and comfortable hip turn, then fold the knee and set down. No high lift or forced crossing start.
e.job: Express the outward hip sweep and its arrest, complementing the inward return action examined in Class 4.
e.gate: Use a bent-knee outward sweep instead if the longer lever causes groin pull or pelvic lean; do not rotate against a fixed support foot.
e.novelty: Outward hip action with added support, opposite mechanical sweep to the earlier inward crescent; not merely the other leg.

e.name: Retreat-step hip-open plant
e.execution: Take one short step backward onto the named leg and open feet/pelvis together into a shallow kick stance. Stop the backward drift within the same 2 m segment and hold 2 s. No kick, run or fast blind travel.
e.job: Retain a usable rotational base while receiving backward bodyweight instead of advancing or moving laterally.
e.gate: Use a shorter, slower retreat instead if the athlete cannot see/control the clear route or heels collide.
e.novelty: Backward receiving momentum and an opening plant; earlier entries arrived forward or laterally.

e.name: Seated self-resisted hip external-rotation acceleration
e.execution: Sit with thighs supported and knee near 90 degrees. The working foot moves a short distance inward as the hip externally rotates; the same-side hand gives very light opposing pressure at the inner lower shin. Accelerate smoothly, then return slowly with knee/pelvis still.
e.job: Give the return-direction hip rotators a small rapid torque task with standing balance removed.
e.gate: Reduce pressure/range instead for any knee/ankle motion or pinching; never jerk into end range.
e.novelty: External-rotation torque with self-resistance, distinct joint action from Class 3 internal-rotation acceleration; four efforts only.

p_jobs: Maintain a challenging planted-leg push with one working round rather than adding fatigue during consolidation.
Preserve posterior-chain strength and controlled stance support at reduced total volume.
Maintain lateral hip/adductor force with one round after the preceding lateral emphasis.
Keep a reproducible direct internal-rotation strength anchor while the explosive task also samples the return direction.
Maintain active chamber-lifting strength without a second round.
Maintain bent-knee ankle force with one working set and full control.
s_jobs: The same easy hip/foot strengthening preserves stable execution conditions while the overall demanding work is reduced.
readiness: Use supported versions and small arcs; the new neutral-start kick still needs qualification. The external-rotation task must move at the hip with a quiet knee. If unfamiliar coordination needs slow instruction, log technique-only attempts rather than insist on full speed.
strength_reason: Reduce Class 5 [1,1,2,1,1,2] to one round per lift [1,1,1,1,1,1]: 76 working reps and 11 working bouts. Relative effort remains challenging at 2–3 RIR; volume is reduced, not replaced by light balance work.
exposure_note: Only four bilateral landings are planned, all from the arms-constrained rotational jump. Twenty-four non-flight efforts include twelve kick/sweep actions. Supported and seated rapid tasks are non-flight efforts, not landing contacts.
space: Most work is stationary; only the short retreat uses up to 2 m plus 2 m recovery space within one 10 m lane. Check the backward path and place nobody behind the receiving athlete.
progression: Following the lateral-entry prescription, this class deliberately halves planned landings from eight to four and reduces strength work from 96 to 76 reps. It consolidates workload and known strength patterns; new drill conditions do not imply skill mastery.
audit: A linked rebound and a second flight drill were rejected for this lower-volume exposure. Support and seated positions reduce balance demands in selected tasks; they still require active rapid force expression and a full reset. The arms-constrained jump is honestly recorded as a variant of the rotational-jump family.
authoring_handoff: Review Class 6 and actual recovery before Class 7; only then qualify any rapid load-to-turn or linked-contact task, with a non-linked same-slot replacement when needed.
current_handoff: Record actual delivery/response and review the next saved class against readiness.
